thread:
deploy-bot: Release candidate 1.12.0 failed dependency-integrity check during pre-canary gating. Details: transitive CVE exceeds policy threshold. SBOM: https://sboms.internal/redwood/release-1.12.0.json

alex.kim: ugh. which package? any exploitability context?

deploy-bot: Transitive dependency: lib-io v2.3.4 -> pulls in parser-x v0.9.1 CVE-2025-0421 (critical, RCE). Policy: block if any critical transitive CVE without mitigations. Full report pasted below.

maria.lopez: ping @security-oncall — we have a canary scheduled at 12:00 PT. do we request an exception or hold?

security-oncall: seeing the report. CVE-2025-0421 has public PoC but only in narrow config; still counts as exploitability present. recommend block unless we can mitigate before canary.

jamal: what are mitigation options today? backport patch? pin to earlier build? rollback to 1.11.3?

qa-lead: 1.11.3 was validated in last window and fits SLA. Rolling back would delay canary but is fastest safe path.

alex.kim: alternatives: (1) pin transitive dep to patched digest in our SBOM and rebuild image, (2) patch-in-HOTFIX to upstream lib-io (unlikely fast), (3) request change-window exemption from compliance + mitigation notes. Rebuild+pin might take ~40m. Rollback ~15m.

maria.lopez: rebuild+pin steps (simple):
```
# in release repo
# update SBOM / lockfile
pkg-lock update parser-x@patched
./ci/build-image --tag candidate-1.12.0-pinned
./ci/run-gate-scans candidate-1.12.0-pinned
```
Expect CI + scans ~30-45m.

security-oncall: if we pin, we need to document mitigation and add runtime WAF rule for the canary as defense-in-depth. Compliance will want that in the ticket.

release-manager: timeline tradeoff: canary at 12:00 PT. If we rollback, we keep schedule. If we pin, canary will slip. What's the business impact?

alex.kim: product said feature is low-risk, not customer-facing launch. I'd prefer safe rollback to keep cadence.

jamal: agree with rollback. I'll open a rollback PR now and trigger a fast canary on 1.11.3 at 12:05 PT.

maria.lopez: @release-manager can you approve rollback plan and notify stakeholders? I'll follow with a postmortem note and the SBOM pin PR to patch for next window.

release-manager: approved. proceed with rollback. notify #prod-updates after canary goes green. Also create a compliance ticket with the CVE report and mitigation plan.

deploy-bot: Rollback PR created: https://git.internal/redwood/release/PR-4821
CI: passing unit tests, integration tests queued.

qa-lead: I'll watch canary runs. if anything flakey, I'll abort and escalate.

security-oncall: once rollback completes, still file SR (security remediation) to track pin+patch for next stable. Add runtime rule until patch lands.

alex.kim: thanks all. tagging :thumbsup: — keeping this thread for final notes.

maria.lopez: Postmortem stub: note transitive CVE, decision: rollback to 1.11.3 to meet change window, follow-ups: backport pin + runtime rule + add transitive CVE scan to PR gates.

deploy-bot: Canary rolled back to 1.11.3 at 12:06 PT. Health checks: OK. Closing gate.
